The Aerosense system uses low-cost, low-power MEMS sensors to measure local pressures and blade motions, and transmits the data wirelessly to a base station.
The absolute pressure sensors can measure pressures from 260 hPa to 1260 hPa with an absolute accuracy of ±50 Pa after calibration.
The differential pressure sensors have a range of -2000 Pa to 2000 Pa with a precision of ±20 Pa, and are used to infer the local inflow conditions.
The hydrostatic pressure variation due to blade rotation can be up to 40% of the aerodynamic pressure on a 5 MW wind turbine.
The influence of centrifugal acceleration on the pressure sensors was found to be negligible for horizontal axis wind turbines, but should be accounted for in vertical axis wind turbines.
Photogrammetry was used to accurately measure the 3D shape and sensor positions on the blade section.
The field measurements on the 7 kW wind turbine showed that the pressure distribution can vary significantly during a single blade rotation, even under stable wind conditions.
The variations in pressure distribution were found to be due to the misalignment between the wind direction and the turbine's rotational axis.
The Aerosense system can provide comprehensive data on the aerodynamic behavior of wind turbine blades, including time-resolved pressure distributions and local inflow conditions.
The Aerosense system is designed to be a cost-effective and easy-to-install solution for the wind energy industry to obtain field measurements and improve blade designs.
